$comment: Perf budgets enforced by pnpm perf (mode ci, GitHub runners) and pnpm perf:ref (mode reference, the M1 Pro reference machine). mw-e32.1. Every number comes from the hardware baseline in docs/backlog-contract.md §1, and each source quotes it verbatim (pnpm perf:budgets checks the quote). Sizes are decimal (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes).

budgets.source: docs/backlog-contract.md §1 Hardware baseline: initial download ≤ 50 MB
budgets.note: Cold load with the cache disabled, everything fetched until playable and the network is quiet.

budgets.source: docs/backlog-contract.md §1 Hardware baseline: initial download ≤ 50 MB
budgets.note: The whole production build (dist/, source maps excluded): a build larger than the initial download cap cannot ship.

budgets.source: docs/backlog-contract.md §1 Hardware baseline: Initial load to playable ≤ 10 s on a 50 Mbps connection
budgets.note: Network throttled to 50 Mbps down through the Chrome DevTools Protocol, cache disabled.

budgets.source: docs/backlog-contract.md §1 Hardware baseline: warm reload ≤ 3 s
budgets.note: A reload right after the cold load, still at 50 Mbps, with the HTTP cache warm.

budgets.source: docs/backlog-contract.md §1 Hardware baseline: JS heap ≤ 1.5 GB
budgets.note: Allocated JS heap (CDP Runtime.getHeapUsage totalSize) after 5 minutes idle in the testbed.

budgets.source: docs/backlog-contract.md §1 Hardware baseline: steady 60 fps
budgets.note: A 200 ms main-thread stall drops 12 frames at 60 fps, which no steady 60 fps run has. GPU-less runners render each frame in software as a 100–200 ms task, so CI counts only long tasks that are not frame renders (overlap no requestAnimationFrame callback: GC, parsing, timers), in the sampling window after the warm-up. All long tasks are reported.

budgets.source: docs/backlog-contract.md §1 Hardware baseline: steady 60 fps
budgets.note: As long-tasks-play, over the 5 minutes idle in the testbed after the first playable frame. Long tasks during loading are reported only.

budgets.source: docs/backlog-contract.md §1 Hardware baseline: steady 60 fps on the reference machine at a 1440p-equivalent render resolution
budgets.note: 60 fps is a 16.7 ms frame interval. 1,800 frames after a 3 s warm-up, uncapped (vsync and frame-rate limit off), 2560×1440 drawing buffer.

budgets.source: docs/backlog-contract.md §1 Hardware baseline: steady 60 fps on the reference machine at a 1440p-equivalent render resolution

budgets.source: docs/backlog-contract.md §1 Hardware baseline: steady 60 fps on the reference machine at a 1440p-equivalent render resolution
budgets.note: On the reference GPU a frame takes milliseconds, so every task of 200 ms or more in the sampling window counts, frame renders included. Same run as frame-p95-high.
